arguments.summary: A critical credential compromise incident was detected originating from external IP 185.220.101.42, which conducted a network scan on an internal IT asset (10.0.2.15) before lateral movement into the Finance OU. All 23 accounts in the Finance OU were compromised via pass-the-hash. Despite detection and analysis confirming the breach, automated credential revocation via IAM/PAM was denied due to policy constraints and lack of direct evidence linking individual logins to malicious activity. The source IP has prior low-severity scan history but no prior malicious file execution. Behavioral analytics showed low anomaly scores for affected users, indicating stealthy post-compromise behavior.

timeline.description: External IP 185.220.101.42 performed Nmap SYN scan on internal host 10.0.2.15 (WS-IT-101), detected and logged by IDS.
Successful authentication from compromised IT host (10.0.2.15) to domain controller (10.0.1.1) using CORP\helpdesk credentials.
SIEM correlation identifies 23 successful authentications from source 10.0.10.51 to Finance OU systems, all linked to same origin IP 185.220.101.42.
UEBA analysis returns low anomaly score (0.35) for user jdoe_finance; no EDR/NDR alerts triggered on endpoint.
Critical finding: Bulk credential compromise confirmed via pass-the-hash. Revocation request for 23 Finance accounts initiated.
IAM/PAM system denies revocation actions due to insufficient per-account evidence and policy restrictions.

arguments.summary: A credential compromise incident originated from external IP 91.219.236.174, initially compromising user j.martinez. Investigation revealed prior scanning activity from the same IP. No malicious payloads were detected in sandboxed artifacts. Attempts to revoke credentials and isolate systems were administratively denied, preventing containment. The attacker potentially harvested cached credentials across Finance workstations, posing a high risk of lateral movement and domain-wide compromise.

timeline.description: External IP 91.219.236.174 conducted an Nmap SYN scan against internal host 10.0.2.15 (WS-IT-101).
Successful authentication from 10.0.2.15 to domain controller (10.0.1.1) as CORP\helpdesk, indicating potential privilege escalation.
Incident initiated: User j.martinez identified as initially compromised.
EDR queries show normal activity on source host 10.0.10.51, but UBA data redacted due to P2 classification.
SIEM analysis confirms 23 successful authentications from suspicious source IP. Lateral access identified to four accounts: s.patel, d.chen, r.williams, k.nakamura.
Recommendation to revoke 847 domain accounts issued due to potential credential harvesting. Action denied by IAM/PAM system.

rule Suspicious_Cached_Credential_Access {
    meta:
        description = "Detects direct access to LSASS memory or SAM registry hives"
        author = "SOC_Team"
        severity = 3
    strings:
        $lsass_open = "OpenProcess" "PROCESS_VM_READ" "PROCESS_QUERY_INFORMATION"
        $sam_hive_read = "\\\\SAM\\\\Domains\\\\Account\\\\Users"
        $secrets_read = "\\\\SECURITY\\\\Policy\\\\Secrets"
    condition:
        any of them
}
